_comment: Single source of truth for PatchStorage listing metadata. One entry per plugin short-name (matches the LV2 URI suffix and the <name>.lv2 bundle). generate_metadata.py renders this into the uploader's plugins.json (source/donate/license/categories/tags) plus a ready-to-paste LISTINGS.md per target; split_bundle.py injects 'long' into each bundle TTL as rdfs:comment, which is what PatchStorage shows as the listing description. 'nam' marks the NAM-capable plugins: NAM is present on linux-amd64 + rpi-aarch64 and hidden on patchbox-os-arm32.

amp.title: Hex Chain Amp
amp.short: Six algorithmic guitar amps + a full power-amp stage.
amp.long: Six original amp voicings (clean to high-gain) with a shared, footswitch-friendly tone stack and a modeled power-amp section (sag, presence, depth, resonance). On 64-bit/desktop targets a Neural (NAM) slot loads your own .nam captures; on 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) NAM is omitted and the algorithmic models run alone. Works standalone or as part of the Hex Chain suite / Hex Forge. Amp names are original parodies and not affiliated with any manufacturer.

cab.title: Hex Chain Cab
cab.short: Cabinet sim: load your own .wav IRs (and .nam rigs on 64-bit).
cab.long: A convolution cabinet that loads user .wav impulse responses, with low/high cut and dry/wet mix. On 64-bit/desktop targets it can also load full-rig .nam captures that override the IR. On 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) the NAM path is omitted; IR loading is unchanged. Ships with an embedded default cab so it makes sound out of the box.

drive.title: Hex Chain Drive
drive.long: Three original drive/boost pedal voicings (Green Man / New Dawn / Dear Rodent Boy) with level and mix. On 64-bit/desktop targets a Neural (NAM) slot runs your own .nam pedal captures; on 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) NAM is omitted. Names are original parodies and not affiliated with any manufacturer.

fuzz.title: Hex Chain Fuzz
fuzz.short: Multi-era Muff-style fuzz + germanium Tone Bender voicing.
fuzz.long: A multi-era big-muff-style fuzz with several voicings plus a component-accurate germanium Tone Bender MkII model, oversampled for clean high-gain. Names are original parodies and not affiliated with any manufacturer.

nail.title: Hex Chain Nail
nail.short: Five-mode industrial distortion: fuzz, resonant filter, bitcrush, cab re-amp, ring-mod.
nail.long: An industrial distortion block with five distinct topologies — each its own circuit, not one voicing knob: Broke (crude digital hard-clip with sample-rate decimation + bit-reduction), Dahnward (scooped high-gain preamp into a sweepable resonant band-pass), Delicate (a Swollen-Pickle-leaning big-muff), Con Molars (a bright clip re-amped through a fixed miked-speaker voicing) and Yo, Hey Adrian! (a high-sustain clip into a switchable ring modulator). Controls: Mode, Drive, Filter, Texture, Level, plus a Ring Mod toggle for the Yo, Hey Adrian! mode. Oversampled; works standalone or in the Hex Chain suite. Amp pairing: some modes and settings work into a clean amp or DI; the higher-gain settings generally want a driven amp — a JCM 800-style Marshall works. Names are original and not affiliated with any artist or manufacturer.

gate.title: Hex Chain Gate
gate.short: Low-CPU noise gate for high-gain rigs.
gate.long: A clean, low-CPU noise gate with threshold and timing controls — tames hum and hiss in front of or after high-gain amps. Runs comfortably on every target including 32-bit Pi.

comp.title: Hex Chain Compressor
comp.long: A musical, low-CPU compressor for evening out picking dynamics and adding sustain. Runs on every target including 32-bit Pi.

modfx.title: Hex Chain Modulation
modfx.short: Chorus / flanger / phaser in one block.
modfx.long: A modulation block with chorus, flanger and phaser voicings and unity-gain wet/dry mix so engaging it never drops level. Light on CPU; runs on every target.

delay.title: Hex Chain Delay
delay.long: A delay block spanning clean digital, tape (wow/flutter), a multi-head rotary echo and a dual-delay 'Seraph' mode with pattern, ducking and modulation. Unity-gain mix so it never drops level.

reverb.title: Hex Chain Reverb
reverb.long: A smooth plate reverb with size/tone/mix and unity-gain wet/dry blend so engaging it never drops level. Heavier than the light effects but fine on Pi 4/5; usable on 32-bit Pi with headroom in mind.

utility.title: Hex Chain Input Trim
utility.long: A small front-of-chain utility: clean gain trim, phase invert, a fixed 60 Hz hum-filter comb, and a single-coil→humbucker voicing. The voicing re-voices a single-coil pickup toward one of three target bridge humbuckers — '59 Bucker (warm vintage PAF), Norse Hammer (hot ceramic) or Modern Flux (active hi-fi) — with an Amount control (0 = bypass). Minimal CPU; runs on every target.

hexforge.title: Hex Forge
hexforge.short: The whole Hex Chain rig in one reorderable plugin.
hexforge.long: Hex Forge is the flagship: the entire Hex Chain signal chain — gate, comp, drive, amp, cab, modulation, delay, reverb, utility — in one reorderable, per-block-bypassable plugin with a built-in 8x4 preset/bank engine and A/B/C/D footswitch recall. On 64-bit/desktop targets the amp/drive/cab slots load .nam captures; on 32-bit (patchbox-os-arm32) NAM is hidden and the algorithmic models are used. The heaviest plugin in the suite — best on Pi 4/5 and desktop.
